title: 2014 HMMT February Geometry Problem 3
statement: \(A B C\) is a triangle such that \(B C=10, C A=12\). Let \(M\) be the midpoint of side \(A C\). Given that \(B M\) is parallel to the external bisector of \(\angle A\), find area of triangle \(A B C\). (Lines \(A B\) and \(A C\) form two angles, one of which is \(\angle B A C\). The external bisector of \(\angle A\) is the line that bisects the other angle.)

solutions.text: \(8 \sqrt{14}\) Since \(B M\) is parallel to the external bisector of \(\angle A=\angle B A M\), it is perpendicular to the angle bisector of \(\angle B A M\). Thus \(B A=B M=\frac{1}{2} B C=6\). By Heron's formula, the area of \(\triangle A B C\) is therefore \(\sqrt{(14)(8)(4)(2)}=8 \sqrt{14}\).
